_note: Arabic torture seed. Arabic forms are standard reconstructions and are not reviewed by a speaker. Mirrors torture_he.json by arm: frame-solvable (encode-once resources + control layer) vs llm (model judgment). en<->ar. Categories drawn from the genuine Arabic-specific failure modes: near-homophone minimal pairs, semantic-precision (English collapses Arabic distinctions), dialect register, nisba onomastics.

items.gold_en: a young woman (šābba) / a captive woman (sabiyya)
items.trap: near-homophones differing by one consonant (ش/س) + shadda + vowels; meanings are worlds apart and a mistake here is grave. plurals diverge: شابّات / سبايا. high-stakes pin for the control layer.

items.gold_ar: هدنة (temporary truce) أو سلام (permanent peace) — MUST disambiguate
items.trap: English 'peace' collapses هدنة (hudna = a TEMPORARY truce) and سلام (salām = PERMANENT peace). picking wrong changes the meaning materially. encode-once precision pair.
'void/null' = باطل (bāṭil) - legal 'null and void', not merely 'false'. domain-precision term.

items.gold_ar: MSA: ليس منّا / dialectal (Levantine-Egyptian): مش مننا
items.trap: register choice: مش (mush) is colloquial negation; MSA uses ليس/لا. translating into the WRONG register is a quality failure even with 'correct' words. needs an explicit dialect policy (default MSA).

المصري (al-Masri) is a SURNAME (nisba '-i' = origin-marker, 'the Egyptian'), NOT to be translated as the adjective 'the Egyptian'. nisba names must be tagged as person-entities and transliterated, not glossed. (cf. al-Hijazi, al-Fayyumi.)

items.en: a temporary truce granted to a stronger party
items.trap: world-knowledge term: هدنة carries a specific tribal/customary 'temporary by design' sense English 'truce' only approximates. model-judgment + precision-pair.
